question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered configuration layers where the earliest layer permanently owns exact paths, with only a closed set of core-defined monotonic policy exceptions?
rationale: Runtime proof establishes that the proposed implementation behaves as documented, but it cannot decide whether this precedence and security authority model should become a permanent supported core contract.

options.title: Approve the V1 contract
options.body: Accept earliest-layer ownership, startup-only immutability, and the narrowly defined tool-policy tightening rules as the supported V1 design.

options.title: Revise the authority model
options.body: Request synchronized RFC and implementation changes to precedence, mutability, or exception semantics before landing.

options.title: Decline core layering
options.body: Keep composition in host-specific tooling if maintainers do not want this compatibility and security contract in OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept earliest-layer ownership, startup-only immutability, and the narrowly defined tool-policy tightening rules as the supported V1 design.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows direct involvement, and the unresolved choice is primarily acceptance of a new core product and configuration contract.
